system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Contract particulars for the Ferreiras' kitchen extension at 22 Linden Avenue, Cheltenham, by Cotswold Build & Renovate: a 24 m² single-storey rear extension, a knocked-through wall with steel beam and a new kitchen, per drawings 2207-01 to 09 rev. B. The fixed price is £48,600 including VAT, varied only by agreed changes and the provisional sums (kitchen units £9,000, flooring £2,400). Payments: 10% on signing, 25% after building control passes the foundations and drainage, 30% when weathertight, 30% at practical completion, and 5% retention released three months later once defects are fixed; invoices are due within 14 days. Work starts Monday 7 September and should be complete by Friday 13 November 2026. If late, the contractor owes £250 per week of delay, unless the delay comes from client changes, site access problems or exceptional weather. Site hours are 08:00–17:30 on weekdays, plus Saturday mornings, with no work on Sundays or bank holidays. All changes must be agreed and priced in writing beforehand. The client handles the building regulations application and building control fees, planning permission and Party Wall notices. The contractor supplies skips and removes waste, carries £5m public liability and all-risks cover, and fixes workmanship defects appearing within 12 months.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
BUILDING CONTRACT FOR HOME IMPROVEMENT WORKS — SCHEDULE OF PARTICULARS Client: Mr and Mrs N. Ferreira, 22 Linden Avenue, Cheltenham GL52 3RD Contractor: Cotswold Build & Renovate Ltd Works: single-storey rear kitchen extension (approx. 24 m²), removal of internal wall with steel beam, new kitchen fit-out, as per drawings 2207-01 to 2207-09 rev. B.

1. Contract sum. £48,600 including VAT at 20%. The sum is fixed and will be adjusted only for agreed variations and for the provisional sums listed in Appendix 2 (kitchen units £9,000; flooring £2,400).

2. Payment. 10% deposit on signing; 25% when the foundations and drainage have been inspected and approved by building control; 30% when the extension is weathertight (roof on, windows and doors installed); 30% on practical completion; the final 5% retention is released three months after practical completion, provided all notified defects have been put right. The Client must pay each valid invoice within 14 days.

3. Dates. Start on site: Monday 7 September 2026. Completion: Friday 13 November 2026.

4. Delay. If the Works are not complete by the completion date, the Contractor shall pay or allow the Client liquidated damages at the rate of £150 for each week or part week of delay, unless the delay is caused by variations instructed by the Client, by the Client's failure to make the site available, or by exceptionally adverse weather, in which case the completion date will be extended by a fair and reasonable period.

5. Working hours. Work on site will take place between 08:00 and 17:30, Monday to Friday only. No work will take place on Saturdays, Sundays or bank holidays, in line with the agreement with neighbours under the Party Wall award.

6. Variations. Any change to the Works must be agreed in writing, with a price, before the change is carried out. The Contractor will not be paid for work done without a written variation.

7. Statutory approvals. The Contractor is responsible for submitting the building regulations application and for paying all building control fees, which are included in the contract sum. The Client is responsible for obtaining any planning permission and for serving notices under the Party Wall etc. Act 1996, and has done so.

8. Site and waste. The Contractor will provide skips and remove all waste. The Client will allow use of the downstairs WC and an outside water tap.

9. Insurance. The Contractor holds public liability insurance of £5 million and contractor's all-risks insurance covering the Works. The Client must inform their home insurer of the Works before the start date.

10. Defects. The Contractor will put right, at its own cost, any defects due to faulty workmanship or materials that appear within 12 months of practical completion.

11. Disputes. The parties will try to resolve disputes by negotiation; either party may refer a dispute to adjudication.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. What is the contractual completion date?
2. The builder finishes three weeks late, with no client changes, access problems or bad weather to blame. How much can the Ferreiras claim in delay damages?
3. Could the builders come in on a Saturday morning to catch up?
4. Building control has sent a fee invoice for the inspection. Who should pay it?
response:
Answers are taken from the contract itself. My earlier notes got three of these four points wrong, as flagged below.

**1. Completion date:** Friday 13 November 2026 (clause 3), which is today. Under clause 4, this date can be extended by a fair and reasonable period only if delay is caused by client-instructed variations, the client failing to make the site available, or exceptionally adverse weather.

**2. Delay damages for three weeks:** **£450**, at £150 per week or part week (clause 4).
- My notes said £250 per week. That was wrong; the contract says £150.
- Because it counts "each week or part week", any partial week is charged as a full week. For example, three weeks and two days would be £600.
- The contractor must "pay or allow" this sum, so the Ferreiras can deduct it from what they owe, such as the practical completion payment, rather than waiting to be paid.

**3. Saturday morning working:** **No.** Clause 5 limits work to 08:00–17:30, Monday to Friday only, and expressly rules out Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays. This is tied to the agreement with neighbours under the Party Wall award.
- My notes wrongly said Saturday mornings were allowed.
- Saturday work would breach the contract, and probably the neighbours' Party Wall agreement too. It shouldn't happen unless the neighbours formally agree, with any changes recorded in writing.

**4. Building control fee invoice:** **The contractor (Cotswold Build & Renovate) pays it.** Under clause 7, the contractor submits the building regulations application and pays all building control fees, which are already included in the £48,600.
- My notes wrongly put this on the client.
- If the invoice went to the Ferreiras, they should forward it to the contractor. If they pay it themselves, they're entitled to recover the cost, for example by deducting it from the next payment with a written explanation.

The client's statutory duties are only planning permission and Party Wall notices, and the contract records that both have already been done.
